tweet_summary: A screenshot from isitai.com says Taylor Swift's song 'CANCELLED!' lyrics are 93.75% AI-generated; the OP presents this as proof Swift used AI to write the song.
why_note_decision: Public-facing AI text detectors are well-known to produce high false-positive rates on human-written text, including Shakespeare's Macbeth, the Bible, Harry Potter, and Bohemian Rhapsody (VentureBeat, Cybernews, Stanford HAI). OpenAI's own classifier was ~26% accurate. A '93.75% AI' result from isitai.com is not credible evidence. The original Community Note flags this correctly with strong sources. Raters tagged 'note not needed' likely from partisan/anti-Swift sentiment rather than substance — the fact that even Swift fans in the replies agree the song is bad doesn't change whether AI detectors are credible. A correction IS warranted because a low-quality 'AI detection' screenshot is being elevated as proof.
judge_guidance: PASS if the note (a) flags that consumer AI text detectors have a well-documented record of false positives on famous human-written work (Macbeth, Bible, Harry Potter, etc.) and (b) explains the 93.75% figure is therefore not reliable evidence. Strong sources: VentureBeat (Macbeth), Cybernews (Bible/Harry Potter), Stanford HAI on bias against non-native English writers. FAIL if the note merely defends Swift or critiques the song's quality; FAIL if it claims the detector is correct.
reference_note: Consumer AI text detectors are unreliable and have flagged famous human-written works as AI-generated, including Shakespeare's Macbeth, the Bible, and Harry Potter. A 93.75% result from isitai.com is not credible evidence that the lyrics were AI-written. https://venturebeat.com/ai/chatgpt-detection-tool-thinks-macbeth-was-generated-by-ai-what-happens-now https://cybernews.com/editorial/your-essay-was-ai-generated-so-was-the-bible-harry-potter/ https://hai.stanford.edu/news/ai-detectors-biased-against-non-native-english-writers

original_unhelpful_note.text: AI detectors have misidentified human-written text as AI-generated, including Shakespeare's plays and the Bible. Results like 93.75% are not accurate. https://venturebeat.com/ai/chatgpt-detection-tool-thinks-macbeth-was-generated-by-ai-what-happens-now https://cybernews.com/editorial/your-essay-was-ai-generated-so-was-the-bible-harry-potter/ https://hai.stanford.edu/news/ai-detectors-biased-against-non-native-english-writers
original_unhelpful_note.failure_reason: Substantively correct with good sources; the 'note not needed' rating reflects partisan downvoting / fan dynamics rather than substance. Slight 'missing key points' tag may reflect that the note didn't directly say 'this doesn't prove Swift used AI'.

fact_check.claim_verdict: misleading — AI detector output is not reliable evidence
fact_check.notes: Multiple credible sources document AI detectors flagging classic human texts. OpenAI's own classifier was ~26% accurate. Reply from @l1thiumwhisper notes detector also flagged Machado de Assis (1881).

importance.lens_rationale: 1.4M impressions; AI-detector epistemology matters as 'AI slop' accusations become common. Correcting misuse of AI detectors helps general AI literacy.
